issues.legal_issue: A court cannot divide a single tenancy let for both residential and non-residential purposes and order eviction under the residential-requirement ground only from the part used as a residence.
material_facts: The premises were let under a single tenancy for both running a school and residence.
The landlord sought eviction on the ground that the premises were bona fide required for his own residence.
The lower appellate court found that the letting was for both residential and non-residential purposes.
The High Court directed that the residential portion be demarcated and that eviction be ordered in respect of that portion.
issues.conclusion: The court lacked jurisdiction to divide the single tenancy and order eviction of the residential portion under the residential-requirement ground. The appeal was allowed, the High Court’s order was set aside, and the decree dismissing the eviction suit was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Section 13(1)(e) of the Delhi and Ajmer Rent Control Act, 1952 permits eviction for a landlord’s bona fide residential requirement only where the premises were let for residential purposes; it does not apply to premises let for composite residential and non-residential purposes. In the absence of statutory authority, a court cannot divide a single, indivisible contract of tenancy and grant relief for only a part of the premises. The court followed Dr. Gopal Das Verma v. S. K. Bhardwaj, [1962] 2 S.C.R. 678, approved Kunwar Behari v. Smt. Vindhya Devi, A.I.R. 1966 Punjab 481, and overruled Motilal v. Nanak Chand, (1964) Punj. L.R. 179.

rule.if: rent_control_eviction_proceeding and landlord_seeks_residential_requirement_eviction and premises_let_for_composite_purposes and tenancy_is_single_and_indivisible and court_proposes_to_separate_residential_portion

predicates.rent_control_eviction_proceeding: The dispute is an eviction proceeding concerning premises occupied by a tenant under rent-control protection.
predicates.landlord_seeks_residential_requirement_e: The landlord seeks eviction on the ground that the premises are required for the landlord’s own residence or that of the landlord’s family.
predicates.premises_let_for_composite_purposes: The premises were let for both residential and non-residential purposes.
predicates.tenancy_is_single_and_indivisible: The parties entered into one tenancy contract covering the premises as a whole.
predicates.court_proposes_to_separate_residential_p: The court proposes to divide the premises and order eviction only from the portion used for residence.

issues.definition: When a rent-control eviction proceeding involves a landlord’s residential-requirement claim, premises let for both residential and non-residential purposes under one indivisible tenancy, and a proposed division of the residential portion, the court lacks jurisdiction to grant partial residential eviction.
